name: Visual Pathways and Field Defect Localization

reference.source: Clinical Neuroanatomy Made Ridiculously Simple / Walsh and Hoyt Clinical Neuro-Ophthalmology
clinicalPearls: Nasal retinal fibres decussate at the optic chiasm; temporal retinal fibres stay uncrossed
Pituitary adenoma compressing crossing central chiasmal fibres produces bitemporal hemianopia
Meyer loop sweeps anteriorly through the temporal lobe; lesions produce pie in the sky superior quadrantanopia
Parietal optic radiation lesions produce inferior quadrantanopia (pie on the floor)
Occipital calcarine cortex infarction produces homonymous hemianopia with macular sparing due to collateral MCA supply
reference.pathophysiology: Retinal photoreceptors transduce photons into electrical signals relayed through optic nerves, chiasm and optic tracts to the lateral geniculate nucleus. Geniculocalcarine fibers project via temporal (Meyer loop) and parietal optic radiations to primary visual cortex. Compressive or ischemic lesions along this pathway produce pathognomonic visual field deficits.
additionalInvestigations: Contrast-enhanced MRI brain and sella for optic pathway lesions
Optical coherence tomography (OCT) of retinal nerve fiber layer
